title: The overeager counter
prompt:
This countdown should print `n` down to `1`, one number per line, and stop. Run it with the `5` in the stdin box and look closely at the output: it goes one line too far.

The loop's exit test is the culprit. Fix the condition so the countdown ends where it should, and leave everything else alone.

## what is checked

- exactly five lines, `5` down to `1`
- the program exits cleanly
- the countdown still comes from the loop
- the same holds for other starting values you do not see; a start of 0 or below prints nothing at all
starter:
// count down from n to one, one number per line
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(i_r, x19)

        .data
fmt_in:     .string "%lld"
fmt_out:    .string "%lld\n"

        .bss
        .balign 8
start_m:    .skip 8

        .text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // read where the countdown starts
        ldr     x1, =start_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =start_m
        ldr     i_r, [x9]
loop:
        cmp     i_r, 0
        b.lt    done                        // stop once i_r runs out
        ldr     x0, =fmt_out
        mov     x1, i_r
        bl      printf
        sub     i_r, i_r, 1
        b       loop
done:
        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
